correctness.rationale: With the cyclic list rooted at a uniformly chosen sampled point (equivalently, at a fixed sample label), the gaps have the Dirichlet(1,…,1) law; homogeneity removes the common exponential normalization. Independently recomputed the four probabilities as exact simplex-volume ratios: eliminate the last gap by sum x_i=1, intersect the simplex with the three linear triangle inequalities from each tested window, enumerate feasible vertices by full-rank active systems, and recursively cone each face boundary from its vertex barycenter. The sums of absolute simplex determinants in dimensions 2, 3, 4, 4 give 1/4, 1/9, 2/27, 232/4725 respectively (the last polytope has ten vertices). Dividing the last result by 1/9 gives 232/525. Disjoint windows depend on disjoint exponentials. For n≥5, exactly two ordered partners per index have each of the two nonzero covariance values 7/144 and 5/432; n=4 has twelve ordered pairs sharing two gaps and n=3 has identical indicators. This gives all variance cases stated. The bounded two-dependent linear sum satisfies Lindeberg using length floor(n^(1/3)) blocks separated by two deleted terms; the deleted variance is o(n), the retained asymptotic variance is 133n/432, and at most two boundary terms change under cyclic closure.
residual_risks: The local indexed probabilities use a sample-point root, not a gap selected by the position of a fixed external angular origin. The count is invariant under cyclic rerooting. No formal proof or exhaustive check outside the stated model is claimed.
